stories.head: True Anomaly secures $190M Series C
stories.body: True Anomaly has raised $190M in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6B as it focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness. The funding is a strong indicator of the DoD's growing interest in commercial solutions for national security. With this cash influx, True Anomaly is well-positioned to capitalize on increasing demand for advanced space capabilities.
stories.soWhat: In a space sector where cash often trumps innovation, True Anomaly's funding underscores the DoD's preference for proven players over risky startups.

stories.head: Anduril and L3Harris team up for SDA
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris have joined forces to bid on a tactical Space Development Agency constellation, signaling a strategic collaboration in an increasingly crowded market. This partnership aims to leverage Anduril's AI-driven capabilities and L3Harris's extensive experience in satellite communications. The move highlights a trend of consolidation as companies seek to pool resources for competitive advantage.
stories.soWhat: As competition heats up, expect more partnerships like this; in space, two heads might not just be better than one, but necessary for survival.

stories.head: Hypersonic glide-vehicle tests slip again
stories.body: Hypersonic glide-vehicle tests have been delayed for the third consecutive quarter, raising concerns about the timeline for this critical defense technology. With the U.S. facing increasing pressure from adversaries, these setbacks could hinder strategic advancements. The repeated delays suggest a systemic issue in the development process rather than just a minor hiccup.
stories.soWhat: If the U.S. can't get its hypersonic act together, the race will be less about speed and more about catching up.

watchlist.title: Watch for True Anomaly's next moves
watchlist.body: With $190M in fresh capital, True Anomaly's strategy will be key to watch as it seeks to expand its market presence.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser progress

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
